pr_title: workload/schemachange: add comma syntax in workload
pr_body:
This patch expands the schema change workload to add support for `ALTER TABLE` statements (`DROP COLUMN`/`ADD COLUMN`/`ALTER PRIMARY KEY`) that have been enabled with our "comma syntax".

Fixes: #122249
Fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/74084

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/122935)
Opening this up for comments -- the comma syntax keeps choosing non-existing tables; so, this still needs one more bit of polishing
closing this in favor of a new PR; the comments/commits of this PR are outdated and largely addressed by https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/127271

issue_context.title: sql/schemachanger: deal with multiple column additions in a single ALTER TABLE
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We currently don't test this much. We need to test this as it's the most complicated thing that we do technically support.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The immediate step is to disable this in the default case. The follow-up is to test this extensively. 

Relates to #59788.

Epic: CRDB-19158

Jira issue: CRDB-11910
comments: Would it be sensible to ignore this in favour of the more general case of schema changes in explicit transactions? Whether the ADD COLUMNs occur (1) in the same statement or (2) in two different statements in an explicit transaction shouldn't matter.
I don't have strong feelings. I agree they are related problems.
